You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Build grids in Python, never hand-type.

task-f8727c1a SOLVED (0 demos, 0 wrong this instance; rule also validated on 3 demos from a prior instance).

FAMILY 'two-panel comparison': input = two same-size panels separated by a constant separator line/column of ONE repeated color (the separator color appears ONLY in the separator, count == panel height/width). Panels may be side-by-side (separator column) or stacked (separator row).

RULE (confirmed on all 3 demos + test): output has the same dimensions as ONE panel. Output background = the SHARED color: the unique color that appears in BOTH panels' palettes (it is noise in one or both panels, bg in the other, e.g. test: left bg 9 / noise 7, right bg 5 / noise 9 -> shared 9). Every output cell = shared color, EXCEPT 3 where BOTH panels have the shared color at that cell: out[r][c] = 3 if panelA[r][c]==shared and panelB[r][c]==shared else shared.

Pitfalls:
- Separator detection: pick the constant line whose color count == line length (appears nowhere else). A constant column of the panel's own bg color exists inside panels and breaks naive 'first constant column' detection.
- Compute shared color as set(panelA colors) & set(panelB colors); it is always a single color in this task.
- Output uses only the shared color and 3; other colors never appear.
---
